prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with knee injury after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 18 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1432; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with right knee pain and swelling. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the kind and force of the impact observed. Initial examination revealed effusion and tenderness along the medial joint line, with positive findings on the valgus stress test, while other ligamentous and neurovascular assessments returned within normal limits. Imaging was reviewed and did not show acute fracture. No prior injury to the right knee is documented in the available history. Care was delivered over 18 visits consisting of physical therapy, anti-inflammatory medication, and activity modification. Treatment followed a typical progression, with visit frequency tapering as range of motion and pain improved. Billed services reflect the planned course of care, with no duplicate or repeated charges identified. At last follow-up the patient was improving and was discharged to a home exercise program with instructions to return if symptoms worsen.
